issues.description: Constructor signature for class SealSaloon is inconsistent between the problem statement and the code examples. The UML and text in problem_statement.md specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name (see UML at line 29 and text at lines 71-73). However, both the template example in Main.java and the reference implementation use and instantiate a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (Main.java: instantiation at line 11; SealSaloon.java: no-arg constructor at lines 8-10 in the solution). This mismatch leaves students unclear which constructor signature to implement and may cause compilation errors or API confusion when they follow different artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(), or (B) change the template Main.java and the reference solution to instantiate and implement SealSaloon(String name) (and update the constructor in SealSaloon.java accordingly). Optionally provide both constructors (SealSaloon() and SealSaloon(String)) to avoid ambiguity, and update all examples and the UML to match the chosen API.

issues.description: The intended declaration and initialization semantics for the stock attribute of SealSaloon are inconsistent in the problem statement. The descriptive text around lines 71-73 suggests initializing attributes (including stock) in the constructor as instance fields, while a later note explicitly states the stock attribute must be static and shared across instances (lines 78-82). The reference implementation declares stock as a static final field initialized at declaration (solution SealSaloon.java at line 5). This contradiction (instance vs static) can confuse students about whether to declare stock as static and how to initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and unify the specification: explicitly state whether 'stock' is an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field shared across all SealSaloon instances. If it is shared, update the problem text to recommend declaring it 'private static final Stock stock' and show initialization at the declaration or in a static initializer. Update the UML, examples (Main.java), and template instructions to match the chosen design so students implement the correct field type.
